# The SQLSTATE corpus, enumerated, and why no scanner came out of it

The fourth review offered a widening with a fact behind it: read a five-character
SQLSTATE token out of a migration comment and measure it against what the database
answers. Verified rather than taken, and it does not hold up. The numbers are here
because a count in a comment is wrong at the next migration, and this one already
was: it changed while F83 was being repaired.

The corpus. A token is a five-character run of digits and uppercase letters carrying
at least one digit, not adjoined by an identifier character, inside a `--` comment of
a migration in supabase/migrations. Before this round: 28 comment lines, 29
occurrences, 9 distinct codes (0A000 2, 23502 1, 23503 10, 40001 1, 40P01 1, 42501 8,
42809 2, 42P10 3, 55000 1), one line carrying 42809 twice. The review said 28 tokens
across eight distinct codes: the 28 reproduces as lines rather than occurrences, and
the ninth code is 0A000, which its phrase "five-digit" excludes. After this round: 29
lines, 30 occurrences, 10 codes, because part 5 now says 23001 beside the statement
and 23502 in the sentence recording what it used to say.

What a scanner would report. Nine of the 29 state a code the database no longer
answers for the statement their sentence names, and eight of those nine are true of
what they describe: five are the before-and-after measurement a section writes to
justify itself (referential_integrity 129, 505, 584, 638, 668 and erased_tenant_ids
402), and three are present-tense statements of what a key buys where the trigger
above it now fires first (referential_integrity 122, 662, and the same shape at 505).
Measured as service_role in a rolled-back transaction on the delivered stack: the
catalogue rename answers 23001 and `update public.tenants set tenant_id` answers
23001, where the sentences say 23503 by the keys. Exactly one of the nine is wrong,
which is F83. A scanner measuring each code against what the database answers now
reports nine and is right about one.

Why that is not shippable. Telling the eight from the one means deciding whether a
sentence is about the delivered statement or about the layer underneath it, which is
a tense and a subject read out of English. That is the same guess
WITHDRAWN_SHAPE_CLAIMS declines for the denial of an index and for the noun phrase
inside a `comment on table`, and the reason is the same: a guard whose report cannot
be trusted is worse than none, because it is read as coverage. So F83 is repaired in
the migration and held as a sentence in WITHDRAWN_SHAPE_CLAIMS, which is the fallback
the return named, and the reasoning is written beside the list rather than left for
the next round to re-derive.

What is measurable in this class and is already built: the assertion in the suite that
runs the statement and prints the code the database gave it. Eight of the ten codes in
the corpus are asserted that way somewhere in packages/core/db.
